full_source_reviews.title: KV-PRM: Efficient Process Reward Modeling via KV-Cache Transfer for Multi-Agent Test-Time Scaling
full_source_reviews.evidence_level: Exact paper v1 with theory, author experiments and appendices; no public author implementation artifact located

method: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.09153v1#S4.SS1 — single verify-token readout over generation KV
https://arxiv.org/html/2607.09153v1#S4.SS2 — LoRA-trained reward head and scoring flow
evaluation: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.09153v1#S5.SS3 — smaller text verifier and verify-token-count controls
https://arxiv.org/html/2607.09153v1#S5.F3 — GH200 latency and memory measurement
https://arxiv.org/html/2607.09153v1#S6 — KV Steering proof of concept
limitations: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.09153v1#S8 — same-architecture requirement, theoretical assumptions and preliminary steering
locators.artifact: No author repository or immutable event-time code artifact is linked in exact v1; RLHFlow/RLHF-Reward-Modeling is a cited baseline, not KV-PRM provenance

full_source_reviews.problem: Long test-time search repeatedly scores partial trajectories. A text PRM re-tokenizes and re-encodes the same growing history for every branch/step, so verifier cost can approach generation cost and scales poorly with trajectory length.
full_source_reviews.old_solution_and_constraint_change: An independent text verifier is a sound default because it has a portable text interface, can use a different model and does not depend on ephemeral generator state. It becomes expensive when long trajectories are scored many times and the generator has already materialized the same prefix as KV state.
full_source_reviews.mechanism: Keep the generator's exact KV cache alive at the scoring boundary, switch to a compatible LoRA verifier adapter, append one verify token, attend that query over the existing K/V, and map the next-token logits for '+' and '-' to a process score. The readout advances only a query token rather than re-running a length-L prefill. The paper also explores differentiating through KV for steering, but that branch is preliminary and must not be merged with the verified read-only scoring mechanism.
full_source_reviews.state_ownership_and_flow: The generator/runtime owns allocation, positions, layout and lifetime of the KV object. The PRM adapter owns the score readout, not the cache truth or final correctness. Transfer/reuse is legal only when base architecture, checkpoint, tokenizer, adapter layout, RoPE/positions, dtype and cache layout are compatible. Search owns branch identity and must prevent a verifier read or experimental steering write from corrupting another branch. Evaluation/decision policy owns how a score influences pruning and must remain separable from executable or outcome truth.
full_source_reviews.tradeoff_and_failure_modes: Representation reuse removes redundant prefill and can retain information not recoverable from decoded tokens, but couples verifier deployment to the generator architecture/state format and extends KV lifetime, memory pressure and access scope. Stale/mismatched KV may produce fluent scores rather than crashes. A reward readout can be miscalibrated or share the generator's blind spots; theoretical richness under assumptions does not prove causal correctness. Steering mutates latent state without a human-readable handoff and can reward-hack the PRM. Independent text verifiers remain preferable across heterogeneous models, remote trust domains, discarded caches, unsupported layouts or high-risk independent review.
full_source_reviews.evaluation_contract: Compare policy log-prob, text PRM and KV-PRM inside the same search procedure; retain per-task accuracy and relative score-computation cost rather than treating FLOP ratios as end-to-end agent speedups. The experiments use Qwen3 0.6B/4B/8B variants on MATH, GSM8K and AIME, with beam search, MCTS and weighted voting. Training appendix reports max length 8192, global batch 2048, BF16 and LoRA rank 256/alpha 32/dropout 0.05. Figure 3 discloses one NVIDIA GH200 120GB GPU; for Qwen3-8B at L=4096, the author reports 4.6 ms versus 172.0 ms for one scoring call. Training hardware, serving concurrency and tail latency SLO remain Not Disclosed, so 15-37x latency, up to 5000x FLOPs and 34.2x per-sequence memory remain author-configuration results rather than end-to-end agent speedups.

benchmark_contract.model: Qwen3-0.6B, Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B generator/PRM configurations
benchmark_contract.hardware: NVIDIA GH200 120GB GPU for Figure 3 latency/memory; training hardware Not Disclosed
benchmark_contract.precision: BF16 training; LoRA rank 256, alpha 32, dropout 0.05
benchmark_contract.input_length: Training maximum 8192; Figure 3 includes L=4096; benchmark trajectories vary
benchmark_contract.output_length: Variable reasoning trajectories; single verify token per score, with k-token analysis as an ablation
benchmark_contract.batch_or_concurrency: Training effective global batch 2048; Figure 3 is a per-sequence/single scoring-call measurement; production inference/search concurrency Not Disclosed
benchmark_contract.evaluator: MATH/GSM8K/AIME answer correctness under reported search algorithms; PRM score is a selection proxy, not outcome truth
benchmark_contract.claim_boundary: Author experiments on same-architecture Qwen3 setups. The 4.6 ms versus 172.0 ms measurement is Qwen3-8B, L=4096, on one GH200 120GB GPU; headline FLOP, latency and memory ratios are not portable constants and do not include a public artifact or heterogeneous/verifier-service deployment.

full_source_reviews.theory_boundary: The capacity argument relies on the Linear Representation Hypothesis; diminishing-return/readout claims add a low-rank reward-structure assumption. KV containing at least as much information as decoded text does not prove a trained one-token readout recovers every reward, nor that its probability is calibrated or independent.
full_source_reviews.books_patch_proposal: In Ch45 after Prefix reuse/correctness identity, add a new consumer branch: generation-only KV -> compatible downstream readout -> verifier score. Explain that reuse can avoid full re-prefill but turns model/checkpoint/adapter/tokenizer/RoPE/dtype/layout/branch position and cache lifetime into a cross-component contract. Separate read-only score from experimental KV mutation; preserve independent text verifier as the compatibility/independence branch. Ch66 and Ch82 already own score authority, verifier independence and branch state; record them as adjacent chapters reviewed, with no duplicate source-specific prose.
full_source_reviews.suggested_patch_text: KV 不一定只能被下一 token 的生成器消费。当同一条 trajectory 需要被频繁评分时，最直接的旧方案是把文本交给独立 verifier 重新 Prefill；它接口稳定、允许异构模型，也保留一定错误独立性，但会重复计算已由 generator 形成的历史表示。另一分支让 compatible verifier 直接读取仍存活的 generation KV：在相同 base architecture 上切换经过训练的 adapter，以一个 verify query 对现有 K/V 做 readout，从而把重新编码整个长度 L 的历史改为一次随 L 线性增长的查询。此时 KV 从 request-private acceleration state 演进为受约束的 cross-component evidence carrier；cache identity 必须增加 generator checkpoint、verifier adapter、tokenizer、position/RoPE、dtype/layout、branch lineage 与有效期。Readout 只产生待校准的 reward proxy，不拥有 trajectory truth；跨模型、跨信任域、cache 已释放或需要独立 evidence 时，text verifier 仍然成立。对 KV 做梯度 steering 则是改变状态的另一条 Experimental 分支，必须与只读评分隔离，并接受 reward hacking、不可解释 mutation 和 rollback 审计。
